species.real: Mam Tor means 'mother hill', and its summit is ringed by the banks of a hillfort first built in the late Bronze Age.
species.name: Crumblet

dex.text: A shaly little lump that shivers all the time, in all weathers, and drops bits of itself wherever it goes. Not cold. Just like that.
dex.fact: Mam Tor in the Peak District is called the Shivering Mountain because its soft shale keeps slipping. The main road below it was finally given up in 1979.

species.real: One story says Blue John got its name from the French bleu-jaune, 'blue-yellow', for its bands of colour. It is a pretty story, and nobody has managed to prove it.
species.name: Shivertor

dex.text: A whole hillside in a bad mood, with veins of blue and gold crystal glinting through the cracks. When it shrugs, the valley below gets a new shape.
dex.fact: Blue John, a banded purple, blue and yellow fluorspar, is found naturally only around Castleton, in the caverns at the foot of Mam Tor.
